steps.note: the Pen is in hand and its chip says how to draw
a triangle landed and the pointer came back with it picked, the way every tool that makes something ends (pen-hands-back-walk is the walk about that)
P over the shape that was just drawn: the Pen comes back and the pick comes WITH it, which is the state the whole task is about. Picking the Pen up is how the anchors of a finished shape are reached

steps.contains: Drag a point to reshape this shape
Double click a point to curve it

steps.note: the chip under the canvas has switched from the Pen's line to the path's: with the Pen in hand it names dragging a point and double clicking one, and says a press anywhere else still draws the next shape
the pointer over the top corner: the cue reads grab, so the open hand says this dot is a different press from the shape it sits on, with the Pen in hand
the top point was dragged with the PEN in hand: it moved, the Pen is still the tool, and nothing new was drawn (still two layers)

steps.contains: Drag a lever to bend the curve

steps.note: two clicks on that point turned the hard corner into a smooth bend, with the Pen in hand and no shape started. The chip has moved on to what the picked point can do next
Backspace with a point picked takes THAT point out rather than the whole shape: two anchors left, still two layers
a press away from the points starts the next shape exactly as before: the triangle is let go, the Pen's own chip is back, and one anchor is down

steps.contains: or the outline to add one

steps.note: with Select in hand the chip offers the one gesture the Pen cannot reach: double click the outline to add a point
two clicks on the BOTTOM edge, which runs between two hard corners and so is straight, added a fourth point: the Select-only half of the job still working
